Let $\mathscr{C}$ be an abelian $\mathbf{k}$ -linear category with tensor product, tensor unit, and associativity, commutativity and unit constraints. Let $H$ be an affine group scheme over $\mathbf{k}$. Let $F:\mathscr{C}\to{\mathord{\mathrm{Rep}}}_{\mathbf{k}}(H)$ be a $\mathbf{k}$ -linear exact faithful functor, compatible with the monoidal structure and the various constraints (in the same sense as in Theorem 2.7). Let $G$ be the affine $\mathbf{k}$ -group scheme provided by Theorem 2.7 (for the composition of $F$ with the forgetful functor ${\mathord{\mathrm{Rep}}}_{\mathbf{k}}(H)\to{\mathord{\mathrm{Vect}}}_{\mathbf{k}}$ ) and $\overline{F}:\mathscr{C}\xrightarrow{\sim}{\mathord{\mathrm{Rep}}}_{\mathbf{k}}(G)$ be the corresponding equivalence. Then there exists a unique morphism of group schemes $f:H\to G$ such that the following diagram commutes:

$\textstyle{\mathscr{C}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{\overline{F}}$ $\scriptstyle{F}$ $\textstyle{{\mathord{\mathrm{Rep}}}_{\mathbf{k}}(G)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{f^{*}}$ $\textstyle{{\mathord{\mathrm{Rep}}}_{\mathbf{k}}(H).}$

If $G$ and $H$ are affine $\mathbf{k}$ -group schemes, any $\mathbf{k}$ -linear functor $F:{\mathord{\mathrm{Rep}}}_{\mathbf{k}}(G)\to{\mathord{\mathrm{Rep}}}_{\mathbf{k}}(H)$ compatible with tensor products, the forgetful functors, and the various constraints is of the form $f^{*}$ for a unique $\mathbf{k}$ -group scheme morphism $f:H\to G$.

2.5 Properties of $G$ visible on ${\mathord{\mathrm{Rep}}}_{\mathbf{k}}(G)$

Recall that an affine $\mathbf{k}$ -group scheme $G$ is called algebraic if the $\mathbf{k}$ -algebra of regular functions on $G$ is finitely generated. In this case, the construction of the group of connected components $\pi_{0}(G)$ of $G$ is recalled in [Mi, §XIII.3] or [Wa, §6.7]; this is an affine étale $\mathbf{k}$ -group scheme endowed with a canonical morphism $G\to\pi_{0}(G)$, and $G$ is connected iff $\pi_{0}(G)$ is trivial.

Recall also that an affine algebraic group scheme $G$ over $\mathbf{k}$ is called reductive33 3

Sometimes, the definition of reductive groups allows disconnected groups. All the reductive groups we will consider in these notes will be (sometimes tacitly) assumed to be connected. Note that connectedness can be checked after base change to an algebraic closure of the base field; see [Mi, Proposition XIII.3.8]. if it is smooth44 4

Recall that this condition is automatic if $G$ is algebraic and $\mathrm{char}(\mathbf{k})=0$; see [Mi, Theorem VI.9.3]. paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
